title: Skull-melting crystal puller: silicon grows its own crucible
idea: Borrowed from titanium and zirconia skull melting: a water-cooled segmented copper cold crucible with RF induction holds the silicon melt inside a frozen silicon skin, so no quartz crucible ever touches the melt; a magnetic cusp field stirs and shapes the melt for 300 mm Czochralski pulls. The crucible is permanent and only electricity is consumed.
why: Eliminates the Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible (>80% concentrated, consumed every 1-2 ingots) and yields oxygen-free crystals with fewer thermal donors and leakage-tail defects; costs ~2-3x melt energy, offset by zero crucible spend and longer continuous pulls.

title: Hydrogen-cooled chucks borrowed from turbo-generator cooling
idea: Large power-plant generators are cooled with hydrogen because it conducts heat better than helium; use 1-20 Torr hydrogen as electrostatic-chuck backside gas in etch, CVD and implant tools, with sealed-band chucks, leak-rate interlocks and hydrogen from on-site electrolysis.
why: Backside cooling is the largest fab helium use, and Qatar's ~30% is offline; H2 thermal conductivity (~0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K for He) gives equal or better wafer temperature control at ~1% of helium cost, removing most fab helium demand.

title: Lost-wax cast aluminum wordlines replace CVD tungsten
idea: Like investment casting: fill buried-wordline trenches with a carbon 'wax' placeholder through all high-temperature steps, burn it out with an oxygen-radical ash, then squeeze-cast molten Al-Si-Sc alloy into the voids at ~600 C and high pressure over the TiN gate liner and planarize.
why: Removes WF6 and tungsten (China ~80%) from the densest metal layer in the array and cuts wordline resistance ~1.5-2x, which allows thinner wordlines; uses the most abundant structural metal and no fluorinated precursor.

title: Kintaro-ame candy draw: shrink a macro array into nanopillars
idea: Kintaro-ame candy hides a face in a log that is stretched and sliced. Build a centimeter-scale preform of glass, metal and semiconductor rods laid out as a DRAM capacitor and bitline cross-section, draw it ~10,000x on a fiber draw tower into a fused multi-core rod, then slice it perpendicular into dies whose pillars already have 100:1+ length, and bond them to a transistor wafer.
why: Forms high-aspect-ratio capacitor and contact columns with no EUV, no immersion multipatterning and no C4F6/C4F8 plasma etch (PFAS, high energy); one preform yields kilometers of identical pattern, cutting patterning capital and fluorinated gas per bit by orders of magnitude if registration can be solved.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor foil anodizing makes self-ordered capacitor holes
idea: Aluminum electrolytic-capacitor makers grow porous alumina by anodizing foil; deposit a thick Al film over the access-transistor layer, pre-texture it with a shallow imprint at the landing-pad pitch, and anodize in sulfuric acid at low voltage to grow ordered 40-60 nm pitch pores registered to the texture, then line them with TiN/ZrO2/TiN.
why: Replaces the deepest fluorocarbon plasma etch and its hard-mask stack with a room-temperature wet electrochemical step on abundant aluminum; anodic alumina routinely exceeds 115:1, attacking the capacitor charge wall while cutting PFAS etch gas and etcher energy.

title: Intaglio acid-etching: catalytic metal etch carves 115:1 silicon trenches
idea: Printmakers bite intaglio plates with acid only where the ground is scratched away; metal-assisted chemical etching does the same in silicon: a patterned silver mesh sinks straight down in HF/H2O2, carving capacitor holes in a sacrificial silicon mold at >150:1, after which the silver is recovered electrochemically and the mold is oxidized or replaced.
why: Reaches the AR ~115 needed for more Cs without C4F6/C4F8 plasma (PFAS, high GWP) or high-power RF etchers, near room temperature; silver is recycled in a closed loop.

title: Brewed photoresists: fermentation-made fluorine-free photoacid generators
idea: Use engineered yeast and E. coli the way breweries and pharma ferment: make bio-based aromatic sulfonium cations, camphor- or lignin-derived sulfonic acid anions and chain-scission polymer backbones, giving ArF and KrF resists with no perfluoroalkyl sulfonate PAGs and no fluorinated surfactants.
why: PFAS PAGs and surfactants face restriction and come from a few Japanese suppliers; fermentation lines cost ~$10-50M rather than a large chemical plant and can be replicated anywhere, removing PFAS from the ~25-35 litho layers of a DRAM wafer.

title: R744 car-AC playbook: CO2 replaces Fluorinert in chuck chillers
idea: Automakers moved air conditioning from fluorinated refrigerants to transcritical CO2 (R744); do the same for etch and CVD chuck temperature control by running direct-expansion CO2 microchannels inside the chuck base instead of pumping perfluorinated heat-transfer fluid from separate chillers.
why: 3M ended PFAS fluid production in 2025, stranding Fluorinert/Galden-type chillers; CO2 is non-PFAS and nearly free, and direct expansion removes the secondary loop, cutting chiller energy ~20-30% and enabling -40 C cryo-etch chucks.

title: Dairy-grade plumbing: electropolished stainless and polyolefins replace fluoropolymers
idea: Dairies and breweries run clean-in-place 316L electropolished stainless with passivated chromium-oxide skins; rebuild fab solvent, gas and ultrapure-water distribution from electropolished, ozone-passivated stainless and reserve high-purity polypropylene and polyethylene for acids, removing PFA and PVDF wetted parts.
why: Fluoropolymer piping, valves and tanks are the bulk of a fab's PFAS inventory and a supply risk as PFAS rules tighten; stainless and polyolefins are abundant, domestic and recyclable.

title: Retreaded memory: remanufacture DRAM dies from retired servers
idea: Like truck-tire retreading and auto-part remanufacturing, hyperscalers return 3-5 year old DIMMs to a line that desolders packages by IR reflow, retests at speed, re-bins by retention and speed, and rebuilds them onto new modules with spare dies and sparing-aware firmware for CXL memory-expansion tiers.
why: Every remanufactured GB saves all the wafer, helium, crucible, water and energy of new silicon; recovering 20-30% of retired server DRAM could add percent-level supply within a year with no fab.

title: Veneer peeling: slice twenty thin wafers from one crystal
idea: Plywood mills peel thin veneers from a log; peel 20-50 um device-grade silicon layers from a thick CZ donor by stress-induced spalling or porous-silicon lift-off, bond each onto a reusable or glass handle, and repolish the donor for the next peel, so one prime wafer yields 15-25 device layers.
why: DRAM uses only the top ~5 um of a 775 um wafer; this cuts CZ ingots, quartz crucibles, polysilicon and growth energy per wafer ~10x and removes wire-saw kerf (~40% of each crystal).

title: Gravure-cylinder nanoimprint rolls DRAM honeycomb arrays
idea: Gravure presses print magazines from an engraved rotating cylinder; build a nickel-sleeved cylinder carrying the capacitor and landing-pad honeycomb and roll it continuously across a UV-curable, fluorine-free resist on each wafer, phase-locked interferometrically so every rotation lands on the same array grid.
why: Replaces several ArF-immersion multipatterning or EUV exposures on the array's most repetitive layers with a tool costing ~1/20 of EUV, using no photomask blanks, no tin plasma and ~1/100 the electricity per layer.

title: Net-shape deposition: area-selective ALD as 3D-printing for films
idea: Additive manufacturing puts material only where the part needs it; use intrinsically chemoselective ALD (dielectric growing on TiN but blocked on SiO2 by an inhibitor vapor pulse, Ru or Mo growing only on metal) to build capacitor dielectrics, liners and caps in place, skipping blanket-deposit, litho and etch-back cycles.
why: Each skipped etch-back saves precursor that would be etched away (Hf, Zr, Ru, W utilization often <5%), a mask and fluorinated etch gas; across ~10 deposit/etch-back loops this could cut metal precursor use 30-50%.

title: Overspray recovery: capture and re-refine ALD precursors from exhaust
idea: Paint booths reclaim overspray; fit ALD and CVD forelines with cold-finger condensers and chelating sorbent cartridges that capture unreacted Zr, Hf, Ru, Mo and W organometallics and halides, then return the cartridges to a precursor refinery that strips and redistills them.
why: ALD sends 90-99% of metal precursor to the abatement burner; closing the loop could halve new hafnium, zirconium and ruthenium demand and cut abatement fuel.

title: Mirror-silvering bath grows rutile capacitor dielectric at 80 C
idea: Tollens' silver-mirror chemistry coats any shape from solution; adapt chemical bath deposition of Al/Nb-co-doped rutile TiO2 (k ~80-100) from aqueous titanium peroxo complexes onto a rutile-templating MoO2 electrode, filling 70:1 holes by diffusion instead of vacuum ALD.
why: Reaching k ~70+ breaks the capacitor charge wall without raising aspect ratio, using abundant titanium and molybdenum instead of hafnium, zirconium and ruthenium, in an atmospheric bath with far less energy and precursor waste.

title: Hall-Heroult for silicon: molten-salt electrowinning from sand
idea: Aluminum is won by electrolysis in molten salt; reduce silica pellets electrochemically in molten CaCl2 at ~850 C (FFC-style) or electrodeposit silicon from silica dissolved in chloride melts onto silicon cathodes, then zone-refine the product to electronic grade.
why: Bypasses carbothermic metallurgical silicon (coke electrodes, 11-13 kWh/kg) and the Siemens trichlorosilane process (~50-60 kWh/kg) and its chlorosilane chemistry, cutting feedstock energy by ~50% or more.

title: Welding-bead crystallization builds germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers
idea: A seam weld's moving melt bead resolidifies as one grain; deposit each 3D-DRAM tier as amorphous silicon on oxide and scan a solid-state green laser line across it so the melt zone recrystallizes laterally from a seed via into the tier below, building single-crystal channels tier by tier.
why: Current 3D DRAM plans use Si/SiGe superlattices, exposing a germanium chokepoint (China export controls) and costly epitaxy; seeded laser crystallization needs only silane and a diode-pumped laser (no neon-buffered excimer) and avoids SiGe strain limits on tier count.

title: Swiss-roll capacitors: strained films self-roll into nano-scrolls
idea: Like a wound film capacitor or a jelly roll, deposit a TiN/dielectric/TiN stack on a strained bilayer over a sacrificial layer; releasing it makes the film curl into a tight multi-turn scroll above each cell, multiplying plate area 10-20x with no deep hole etch.
why: Gives 2-5x more Cs per footprint than 70:1 pillars while eliminating the high-AR fluorocarbon etch and its multilayer hard mask (PFAS gas, energy and critical litho for the hole layer).

title: Pharma isolator fab: sealed tool tunnels replace ballroom cleanrooms
idea: Aseptic pharma moved from cleanrooms to sealed isolators; connect DRAM tools with nitrogen-purged sealed transport tunnels and mini-environments so only ~5% of fab volume is ISO-class clean and the rest is ordinary industrial air.
why: Cleanroom air handling and makeup-air conditioning are ~30-50% of fab electricity and much of its cooling water; isolating only the wafer path could cut fab energy ~25%, water ~15% and construction cost.

title: Distillery heat-recovery stills turn fab waste heat into UPW
idea: Whisky distilleries and desalination plants cascade heat through multi-effect stills; route the fab's 30-45 C process-cooling heat into membrane distillation modules that turn reject brine and rinse wastewater back into ultrapure-water feed, approaching zero liquid discharge.
why: A large DRAM fab draws ~20-40 million liters per day; recovering 70-90% of rinse water with free low-grade heat cuts withdrawals at drought-prone sites and RO energy.

title: Calculator-style chip-on-board DIMMs skip the package substrate
idea: Cheap calculators and LED boards bond bare dies straight to the board under a glob-top; mount known-good DRAM dies directly on the module PCB with copper-pillar flip-chip and one over-mold per module, eliminating per-die BT substrates, glass cloth and individual mold caps.
why: Package substrates and low-CTE glass cloth are a separate Japan-concentrated chokepoint; removing them cuts materials and package cost per GB ~10-20% and shortens traces for lower I/O energy.

title: Refinery stripping of chamber shields recovers tungsten and hafnium
idea: Gold refiners strip plated scrap electrochemically; instead of bead-blasting deposits off PVD, CVD and ALD chamber shields into landfill, strip them in selective anodic baths that redissolve W, Mo, Hf, Zr, Ru and Ta, then precipitate and calcine each metal as a pure salt for precursor makers.
why: Chamber kits accumulate a large share of deposited metal (PVD target utilization is only ~30-40%); recovery gives fabs a secondary supply of China-concentrated tungsten and scarce hafnium and ruthenium.

title: MLCC co-firing on a carrier, then transfer the capacitor layer
idea: MLCC makers fire barium titanate layers at ~1100 C on carriers; fire a sub-100 nm relaxor (Ba,Sr)(Ti,Zr)O3 dielectric between conductive-oxide electrodes on a sacrificial carrier wafer, pattern a shallow 5:1 relief, then hybrid-bond and layer-transfer it onto the cold access-transistor wafer.
why: Decouples perovskite crystallization (k 300-1000) from the CMOS thermal budget, so a shallow capacitor reaches ~5 fF without 70:1 holes or hafnium/zirconium ALD; barium and titanium are abundant.

title: Cast-iron skillet seasoning: reusable silicon nitride crucibles for CZ
idea: A seasoned cast-iron pan lasts generations; make CZ crucibles from reaction-bonded silicon nitride (U.S. silicon powder nitrided in U.S. air-separated nitrogen) with a self-renewing Si3N4/SiO2 'seasoning' coat reapplied between pulls, so one crucible serves dozens of 300 mm pulls.
why: Removes dependence on the single Spruce Pine site and on foreign crucible fabricators while making crucibles reusable; nitrogen doping is already prized for vacancy-defect control, turning contamination into a feature.

title: Slip-cast synthetic-silica crucibles from polysilicon plant byproduct
idea: Potters slip-cast vessels from liquid clay; hydrolyze SiCl4 byproduct from a Michigan polysilicon plant into colloidal synthetic silica, slip-cast crucible bodies in porous molds, and arc-fuse them with a synthetic inner wall, all within one U.S. chemical park.
why: Turns a waste stream into crucibles ~10x purer than natural quartz, relieving the Spruce Pine concentration (a 2024 hurricane shut it) and foreign crucible makers; purer crucibles also cut oxygen-precipitate defects.

title: Aircraft-brake carbon composites become crystal puller hot zones
idea: U.S. aircraft-brake plants make carbon/carbon composites by winding PAN fiber and densifying it by chemical vapor infiltration from natural gas; use those lines for CZ heaters, susceptors, heat shields and crucible supports, replacing imported isostatic graphite.
why: Isostatic graphite comes mainly from Japan and China; C/C parts last ~3-5x longer and cut hot-zone heat loss ~15-25%, lowering crystal-growth energy per wafer with an all-domestic chain.

title: Moonshine stills for helium: modular skids on stranded U.S. wells
idea: Like a moonshiner's portable still, skid-mounted membrane and pressure-swing helium purifiers sit on low-volume Kansas, Montana and Arizona gas and nitrogen wells that big plants ignore, filling ISO cryo-containers run on a milk route to U.S. fabs under long-term offtake contracts.
why: Builds a fab-dedicated domestic helium supply independent of Qatar and the large-plant oligopoly; each skid adds ~5-30 Mcf/day, so a few dozen can cover a large DRAM fab.

title: Refinery side-draws: U.S. steel-plant air separators harvest neon
idea: Oil refineries pull extra fractions from column side-draws; add crude rare-gas columns to the big air separation units at U.S. steel mills and chemical plants, purify neon, krypton and xenon centrally, and recycle the fab's ArF/KrF laser exhaust through the same plant.
why: Neon (once ~50% from Ukraine and Russia) gates DUV lithography; a domestic supply plus laser gas recycling secures every exposure in a U.S.-only, no-EUV DRAM flow that relies more heavily on multipatterning.

title: Copper anode slime yields selenium-tellurium p-channel access transistors
idea: Copper refineries recover selenium and tellurium from anode slimes, and Utah produces both; evaporate SexTe1-x films below 200 C as p-channel transistors for BEOL-stacked gain cells, raising the bandgap to ~1 eV with selenium to hold leakage down, paired with an n-type zinc oxide device.
why: Removes indium and gallium (China-concentrated and export-controlled) from stacked oxide-semiconductor DRAM, using a material whose whole U.S. chain already exists as a refinery byproduct.

title: Mist-CVD humidifier grows indium-free zinc oxide channels
idea: Like an ultrasonic humidifier or a spray gun, nebulize aqueous zinc acetate with silicon or aluminum dopant precursors and carry the mist in air onto ~300 C wafers to grow amorphous Zn-Si-O channels for BEOL access transistors, using zinc smelted in Tennessee.
why: Gives a wide-gap (3.3 eV), low-leakage, indium- and gallium-free channel for stacked gain cells with no vacuum, no organometallics and ~1/10 the energy of sputter or ALD lines.

title: Batik dopant-resist stacks make germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers
idea: In batik, wax marks what the dye must not touch; grow an all-silicon stack in which sacrificial tiers are heavily boron-doped and channel tiers lightly doped, then remove the sacrificial tiers laterally with a dopant-selective electrochemical or HNA-type etch, replacing SiGe sacrificial layers.
why: Eliminates germanium (China ~60%, export-controlled) and SiGe lattice strain that caps tier count, enabling 30+ tiers from domestically made silane and diborane.

title: Moly roaster to wordline: Colorado molybdenite becomes a tungsten-free metal
idea: Integrate like a steel mill from ore to coil: roast Climax/Henderson molybdenite concentrate to MoO3, chlorinate it on site to MoO2Cl2 CVD precursor, and deposit fluorine-free molybdenum fill for buried wordlines, bit-line contacts and periphery plugs.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%, no U.S. mine operating) from the whole flow; Mo has lower resistivity than W in narrow lines and the U.S. is a top-three Mo producer.

title: Paint-pigment TiCl4 refined into electronic capacitor electrodes
idea: As sugar refiners turn table sugar into pharmaceutical sucrose, add a fractional-distillation and adsorber polishing train beside U.S. chloride-process pigment plants in Tennessee and Mississippi to make 6N TiCl4 for TiN capacitor electrodes, gate liners and barriers.
why: TiN is in every DRAM capacitor and wordline; this gives a domestic electrode supply at commodity cost, removing imported TiCl4/TDMAT and the pull toward scarce ruthenium electrodes.

title: Manganese-for-nickel stainless playbook: lanthanum replaces hafnium high-k
idea: Steelmakers swapped scarce nickel for manganese in 200-series stainless; swap hafnium in periphery high-k metal gates and capacitor interlayers for lanthanum aluminate and La-doped ZrO2, made from Mountain Pass (California) rare-earth output and deposited by ALD from lanthanum amidinates.
why: World hafnium supply is only ~70-100 t/yr from a few zirconium refiners; lanthanum is the most abundant rare earth with a domestic mine and separation, and LaAlO3 (k ~25) matches HfO2.

title: Overflow fusion-draw glass panels host U.S.-made panel DRAM
idea: Display glass is made by overflow fusion draw in Kentucky; on those 3 m panels, use U.S.-built i-line steppers and PECVD to stack 8-16 tiers of indium-free oxide gain-cell DRAM at ~1 um features, getting density from stacking and panel area instead of shrinking.
why: Needs no silicon wafers, no CZ crucibles, no EUV and no foreign litho; at ~1 um and 16 tiers a panel holds ~100 GB/m^2 at display-backplane cost (~$5/GB), a slow bulk-DRAM tier for CXL.

title: Optical-fiber soot process makes domestic photomask blanks, recycled like cullet
idea: Use New York flame-hydrolysis high-purity fused silica (the soot method behind optical-fiber preforms) as mask substrate, and add a cullet-style reclaim line that strips chrome, repolishes and recoats retired DRAM masks for reuse.
why: Mask blanks are concentrated in Japan; a U.S. source plus 3-5 reuse cycles per blank cuts synthetic-quartz demand and mask cost for the ~60-70 masks a DRAM product needs.

title: Jacquard loom lithography: Texas-made DLP mirrors write periphery layers
idea: The Jacquard loom replaced fixed patterns with programmable punched cards; build maskless exposure engines from Dallas-made DLP micromirror chips with reduction optics and expose DRAM periphery, pad, redistribution and upper-metal layers straight from data.
why: Removes masks and blanks for ~20-30 non-critical layers per product and foreign stepper dependence on those layers, and lets each wafer carry its own repair and redundancy wiring; ~0.3-1 um resolution suffices there.

title: Copper heap-leach playbook: bacteria mine tungsten and gallium domestically
idea: Copper mines pull metal from low-grade heaps with acidophilic bacteria; apply engineered bioleaching heaps to Nevada tungsten-skarn tailings, Appalachian coal fly ash and alumina red mud to dissolve W, Ga and Ge, then recover them by solvent extraction and ion exchange.
why: Supplies U.S. fabs with tungsten, gallium and germanium (all China-dominated and export-controlled) from existing waste piles at low capital; semiconductor demand is small in tonnage, so modest heaps suffice.

title: Foundry-sand reclamation for ceria: closed-loop Mountain Pass CMP slurry
idea: Foundries scrub and recalcine used casting sand; collect ceria CMP waste from trench-isolation and dielectric polishing, hydrocyclone and acid-wash it, recalcine to set crystallite size, and top up with ceria from Mountain Pass, California.
why: Ceria abrasive is a rare-earth product mostly from China; a 70-80% reclaim loop plus a domestic mine makes CMP fully domestic and cuts slurry waste and water.

title: Dry-cleaner wafer benches run on ethanol-plant CO2
idea: Dry cleaners wash clothes in liquid CO2 without water; replace post-etch residue removal and rinse-dry steps with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvent chambers, fed by fermentation CO2 captured at Midwest ethanol plants and recycled in a closed loop.
why: Cuts ultrapure water and IPA on cleaning steps ~50-80%, prevents pattern collapse of 70:1 capacitors, and turns a domestic waste gas into a process fluid.

title: Fertilizer-plant fluorine: Florida phosphate byproduct replaces imported fluorspar
idea: Phosphate fertilizer plants scrub fluorosilicic acid from off-gas and mostly neutralize it; convert it via the bifluoride route to anhydrous HF and then to electronic-grade HF, NF3 and F2 at a Gulf Coast plant, recovering silica as a coproduct.
why: U.S. HF depends on imported fluorspar from Mexico and China; phosphate byproduct could supply all fab fluorine chemistry domestically while keeping it fluorocarbon-free.

title: Steel minimill for silicon: remelt kerf and scrap wafers domestically
idea: Electric-arc minimills make new steel from scrap; build a U.S. silicon minimill that collects wire-saw kerf, broken and spent test wafers and off-spec ingot tops, acid-cleans and plasma-refines them, and directionally solidifies them into CZ recharge feedstock.
why: Kerf wastes ~40% of each crystal; recycling it reduces new polysilicon and its ~50-60 kWh/kg Siemens energy, giving a domestic loop independent of Chinese polysilicon.

title: Pharma flow chemistry: fab-side microreactors brew ALD precursors
idea: Pharma replaced batch kettles with continuous-flow microreactors; synthesize Zr, Hf, Mo and Al ALD precursors beside the fab from Oregon zirconium and hafnium chlorides and Gulf Coast amines in skid-scale flow reactors with inline distillation, delivered by pipe instead of shipped cylinders.
why: Precursors come from a handful of Korean, Japanese and European firms; point-of-use flow synthesis gives a domestic supply, cuts inventory and cylinder logistics, and delivers fresher, purer precursor.

title: Porcelain enameling: borax-glaze BCN barrier replaces tantalum liners
idea: Enamelers fuse borax glazes to steel as impermeable barriers; deposit a ~1-2 nm amorphous boron-carbon-nitride 'glaze' from precursors made from California borax as the copper diffusion barrier and liner in DRAM metal layers, replacing Ta/TaN.
why: Tantalum comes from conflict-mineral regions; a thinner barrier also frees conductor cross-section for ~20-30% lower line resistance at tight pitch.

title: Inkjet-head e-beam writer: 10,000 beamlets pattern without EUV
idea: Inkjet heads fire thousands of nozzles in parallel; build U.S. multi-column electron-beam direct writers with MEMS beam-blanker arrays that write DRAM critical layers straight into resist, replacing EUV exposures with a mask-free step.
why: EUV has one foreign supplier and each tool draws ~1 MW with tin plasma and hydrogen; a domestic multibeam writer removes EUV, masks and pellicles and can write per-wafer redundancy maps.

title: Chlor-alkali cells on site: electrolytic ozone water replaces sulfuric-peroxide cleans
idea: Chlor-alkali plants make chemicals from brine with electricity; put diamond-electrode electrolyzers at each wet bench to generate ozonated water, hydrogen water and peroxide on demand, replacing piranha resist strips and RCA cleans.
why: Removes bulk semiconductor-grade sulfuric acid and H2O2 (short in the U.S. in 2021-22), their trucking and neutralization waste, and cuts chemical and rinse water ~30-50% using only domestic water and electricity.
